issues.title: Single-pipeline resume clears the shared shop block and can release a different previously authorized pipeline which has not reached its signing guard yet
sequence: A and B in the same shop both have process-local authorization; B has not attempted signing after A fails.
A signer throws CANCELLED. guarded() adds BLOCKED_SHOPS[shop] and WAITING_PIPELINES[A], leaving B absent from WAITING_PIPELINES.
The new foreground resumeSigning(A) calls existing authorizePipeline(A), which removes the entire shop from BLOCKED_SHOPS.
B later enters guarded(); it has no WAITING marker and retains its prior authorization (or shop authorization), so work.run() is reached without explicitly resuming B.
issues.evidence: Deterministic static control flow; not a test execution claim. Existing new test authorizingOnePipelineClearsOnlyItsShopCauseAndDoesNotWakeOtherWaitingPipelines first places B in WAITING, so that case does not cover B which has not polled yet.
issues.scope: If the new action is specified to resume exactly one saved lot as its Javadoc states, shared-shop unblocking is wider than that action. Existing authorizePipeline behavior predates this patch; the new resume entry point exposes it as single-lot recovery.
issues.suggestion: Add a regression for an already-authorized but not-yet-WAITING B, then use a scope-specific resume authorization that leaves other shop-blocked signing contexts blocked. Do not broadly change original new-purchase/shop-selection authorization semantics without separate coverage.
